_comment: Template for a machine-local config. Copy to batch.config.local.json, replace @DATA_DIR@ with an absolute folder on local disk (see docs/CONFIG.md), then export TAGSITES_BATCH_CONFIG=batch.config.local.json. Values are for C. elegans; docs/BUILD_LOCAL_DATABASE.md lists what to change for another organism.

backends._comment: analysis -> backend mode; providers.py imports scripts/<analysis>_<mode>.py. Omit an analysis (or set it to "remote") to keep today's EBI/Ensembl behavior.

reference_data._comment: paths/URLs for scripts/reference_data.py's bulk downloads (Phase A). out_dir should point at large external storage.

conservation_local._comment: scripts/conservation_local.py's DIAMOND search targets, each an independent database with its own search params (see scripts/reference_data.py's fetch_swissprot()/fetch_rhabditida_trembl()). Inert unless backends.conservation is set to "local". threads = DIAMOND --threads (also bounds batch_run.max_workers' MAFFT/JSD phase to 16 busy threads); chunk_size = queries per batched DIAMOND call in scripts/conservation_presearch.py; render_alignment_pdf = write the alignment PDF (true for the app; batch runs set false and can render it later from the .aln). Every search runs with --ultra-sensitive (DIAMOND's closest approximation to real BLASTP sensitivity) unless a database entry overrides "sensitivity".

domains_scan._comment: scripts/pfam_scan.py's local de novo Pfam-A scanning knobs (scripts/build_pfam_cache.py's bulk pass and scripts/domains_scan.py's on-demand fallback). Inert unless backends.domains is set to "scan". bit_cutoffs: "gathering" uses Pfam's own per-model gathering thresholds (matches InterProScan); clan_filter drops lower-scoring overlapping hits within the same Pfam clan; cache_profiles keeps Pfam-A's ~21k HMMs loaded in memory after first use (recommended for a long-lived batch worker); cpus: 0 = use all available cores.

deeptmhmm._comment: scripts/deeptmhmm_runner.py's subprocess bridge to DeepTMHMM 1.0 (academic license, vendored outside the repo, not committed here). install_dir/python are machine-specific and left blank in this checked-in default — set them in a TAGSITES_BATCH_CONFIG override (e.g. batch.config.local.json) to the local DeepTMHMM checkout and its dedicated conda env's python (needs pytorch<2.6, fair-esm==0.4.0 — see plan for why). batch_size is scripts/build_topology_cache.py's sequences-per-subprocess-invocation knob, trading ESM1b model-load amortization against peak embedding scratch (deleted after each batch). batch_residues additionally closes a batch at that many total residues (bounds scratch/VRAM for the long isoforms processed last). max_length, if set, skips and logs to topology_cache/_skipped.tsv any sequence longer than that (null = no cap).

proteome_db._comment: scripts/build_proteome_db.py / scripts/proteome_db.py. path = the finished SQLite file (read it with proteome_db.py; it is opened read-only/immutable because SQLite locking is unreliable on network volumes). run_dir = the proteome_run.py output folder to ingest. build_dir = LOCAL disk where the database is assembled before being copied to path (blank = the system temp dir); scratch_dir = where the reagent stage writes its transient per-protein TSVs, deleted after each chunk (blank = under build_dir). chunk_size = proteins per worker task when parsing; curated_sites = JSON lists of known tag sites (gene, wormbase_id, site, flank_n, flank_c) matched to proteins by flanking sequence; reagent_chunk = proteins designed per round of the reagent stage (bounds transient disk: ~6 MB of TSV per protein). app_match = the Shiny app looks a loaded sequence up in this file (exact match) and offers its precomputed results via Setup; it is inert unless the file exists, so the deployed app never shows it. Always run `build_proteome_db.py --estimate` first: it samples, measures each table, and projects the full size and reagent run time without building anything large.

batch_app._comment: app_batch.py (batch review app). batch_dir = LOCAL folder holding every batch (one subfolder each: {name}.batch.json plus one run folder per protein); workers = parallel database exports in Prepare; ebi_max_concurrent = proteins analysed on EBI at once; cache_entries = parsed runs kept in memory for Review (about 3 per protein); port = the app's port (app_modular.py uses 8000).
